artifacts.summary: Confirms by direct code reading that git-commit-scoped.sh's V5 contention check, guard-destructive-git.sh's hook, and the script's own V2 classification all fail to catch a bare directory pathspec; finds 17 occurrences of the `-- specs/` anti-pattern across 3 extensions (not the 3 named in the dispatch), and confirms widening fix scope would not trip the self-modification admission gate.

memory_candidates.content: git-commit-scoped.sh's V5 contended-path check (specs/.contention-manifest/) matches pathspec entries by EXACT STRING EQUALITY (`.path == $p`) against the caller's own literal pathspec token. A directory-shaped token (e.g. `specs/`) can never equal a specific file path, so it silently slips past V5 regardless of manifest contents -- and separately, the manifest is populated only from task file_scope declarations, which essentially never include specs/ artifact paths, so V5 is structurally orthogonal to specs/-artifact cross-task bleed. guard-destructive-git.sh's directory/glob pathspec hook also misses this class: its detector only fires on the literal substring 'git add' in the Bash tool command text, never on a wrapper script invocation like `bash .../git-commit-scoped.sh ... -- specs/`.

When a task description cites a specific count of 'N occurrences' of a code anti-pattern as the basis for a small-effort fix, re-verify the count with a full-tree grep before accepting the scope as given -- in task 309, 'three commit recipes pass a bare -- specs/ pathspec' undercounted the actual source-store footprint (17 occurrences across 3 extensions) by more than 5x. Cross-check against context/reference/orchestrator-critical-paths.json before recommending a scope widening, to confirm it would not trip the self-modification admission gate.
